mainTopic: בן סורר ומורה: the amounts and kinds of meat and wine that make him liable, followed by aggadic teachings on the dangers of wine and the story of נח
overview: The amud opens by finishing the previous discussion: a daughter cannot become a בן סורר ומורה, because the Torah says "בן". A new משנה then sets how much meat and wine he must eat. It rules out eating that is part of a מצוה or an עבירה, and it requires real meat and wine, based on "זולל וסבא". The גמרא works out that a תרטימר is half a מנה. רב הונא adds that the meat and wine must be bought cheaply and be half-cooked and half-mixed. Salted meat and wine fresh from the press do not count. Their time limits differ from the limits for ערב תשעה באב, because the reason behind each law is different. The גמרא then turns to teachings about wine: it comforts mourners, it can raise a person up or ruin him, and it brought "woe" in the story of נח. It discusses what חם did to נח and notes that נח should have learned from אדם הראשון, whose tree some say was a grapevine. רבי מאיר's ברייתא on this continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Only a son, not a daughter, by Torah decree
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes its point: logic might include a daughter, but the Torah's word "בן" limits the law to a son.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since everyone is often found sinning with her, you would think a daughter should be judged too. But it is a decree of the Torah: "a son" and not a daughter.
steps.whatsHappening: This line finishes a discussion from the previous page. The גמרא concludes that a daughter cannot become a בן סורר ומורה, simply because the Torah says "בן".
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reasoning (people are found with her in sin) would make a daughter seem even more fitting for this law. The גמרא sets that logic aside because the Torah's wording decides the case. This is a גזירת הכתוב, a rule we follow because the פסוק says so, not because of a reason.

keyTerms.meaning: a decree of the פסוק; a rule followed because the Torah says so
a son and not a daughter

steps.whatToRemember: בן סורר ומורה applies only to a son. Logic would include a daughter, but the Torah's word "בן" overrides it.

phrases.english: since everyone is commonly found with her in sin,
but it is a decree of the verse:
"a son," and not a daughter.
phrases.notes: דברים 21:18

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the earlier discussion about whether a daughter is included.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A daughter is excluded from בן סורר ומורה by the Torah's explicit word "בן", even though logic might include her.

steps.title: How much meat and wine makes him liable
steps.stepSummary: The new משנה sets the amounts: a תרטימר of meat and half a לוג of Italian wine. רבי יוסי says a מנה of meat and a לוג of wine.
steps.simpleTranslation: From when is he liable? From when he eats a תרטימר of meat and drinks half a לוג of Italian wine. רבי יוסי says: a מנה of meat and a לוג of wine.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It asks at what point the son becomes liable, and gives a minimum amount of meat and wine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being a glutton is measured by real amounts, not by general behavior. The תנא קמא gives smaller amounts. רבי יוסי requires more meat (a full מנה) and double the wine (a full לוג).

phrases.english: MISHNAH:
From when is he liable?
phrases.notes: "He" is the בן סורר ומורה, the son this whole chapter is about.

phrases.english: From when he eats a tarteimar of meat,
phrases.notes: A תרטימר is a weight measure. The גמרא will explain how much it is.

phrases.english: and drinks half a log of Italian wine.
Rabbi Yosei says:
a maneh of meat, and a log of wine.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה about the amounts that make the son liable.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Liability starts at a תרטימר of meat and half a לוג of Italian wine. רבי יוסי requires a מנה of meat and a לוג of wine.

steps.title: Eating that does not count
steps.stepSummary: The משנה lists ways of eating that do not count: eating tied to a מצוה, and eating forbidden foods.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he ate at a מצוה meal, at the meal for adding a month, or ate מעשר שני in ירושלים; if he ate נבילות, טריפות, שקצים or רמשים, or טבל, untithed first tithe, or unredeemed מעשר שני and הקדש...
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה is listing cases. It does not give the ruling yet; the next line will say these cases do not make him a בן סורר ומורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The list has two groups. The first three cases involve eating as part of a מצוה. The rest involve eating forbidden food. Both groups will be ruled out, so the gluttony must be ordinary, permitted eating.

keyTerms.meaning: a group gathered for a מצוה meal
adding an extra day to the month, celebrated with a meal
animals not properly slaughtered, and fatally injured animals
food consecrated to the בית המקדש

steps.confusionAlert: Don't read the first three cases as sins. They are מצוה meals. They don't count because his eating there is connected to a מצוה, not because they are forbidden.

phrases.english: If he ate with a group gathered for a מצוה,
if he ate at the meal for adding a day to the month,
if he ate second tithe in Jerusalem,
if he ate carcasses and tereifot,
disgusting creatures and creeping creatures,
(if he ate untithed produce, or first tithe
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the words in round brackets.

phrases.english: whose terumah was not separated,
or second tithe and consecrated food that were not redeemed).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After setting the amounts, the משנה lists kinds of eating that will not count.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Eating connected to a מצוה, or eating forbidden foods, is listed as not counting. The ruling itself comes in the next line.

steps.title: He must eat real meat and drink real wine
steps.stepSummary: The משנה sums up: eating for a מצוה or an עבירה, or eating other foods and drinks, does not make him a בן סורר ומורה. Only meat and wine do, as the פסוק says "זולל וסבא".
steps.simpleTranslation: If he ate something that is a מצוה or something that is an עבירה, or ate any food but not meat, or drank any drink but not wine, he does not become a בן סורר ומורה until he eats meat and drinks wine, as it says: "a glutton and a drunkard."
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה now gives the ruling for all the cases above. It adds that only meat and wine count, and brings a פסוק as the source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two limits are set together. First, the eating must be neither a מצוה nor an עבירה. Second, it must be meat and wine specifically. The source is the Torah's description of the son as a "זולל" (glutton) and "סובא" (drunkard).

keyTerms.meaning: glutton, here meaning an eater of meat
drunkard, here meaning a drinker of wine

steps.whyThisMatters: This defines the act that makes the son liable. It is not just any overeating, but a specific kind of meat-and-wine gluttony.

phrases.english: If he ate something that is a מצוה,
or something that is a sin,

phrases.aramaic: אָכַל כׇּל מַאֲכָל וְלֹא אָכַל בָּשָׂר,
phrases.english: if he ate any food but did not eat meat,

phrases.aramaic: שָׁתָה כׇּל מַשְׁקֶה וְלֹא שָׁתָה יַיִן –
phrases.english: if he drank any drink but did not drink wine –
he does not become a stubborn and rebellious son
until he eats meat and drinks wine,
as it is stated: "a glutton and a drunkard."
phrases.notes: דברים 21:20

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵינוֹ נַעֲשֶׂה בֵּן סוֹרֵר וּמוֹרֶה עַד שֶׁיֹּאכַל בָּשָׂר וְיִשְׁתֶּה יַיִן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the ruling for the list in step 3 and adds that only meat and wine count.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: He becomes a בן סורר ומורה only by eating meat and drinking wine, when the eating is neither a מצוה nor an עבירה, based on "זולל וסבא".

steps.title: A hint from משלי that זולל and סובא mean meat and wine
steps.stepSummary: The משנה admits there is no full proof that "זולל וסבא" means meat and wine, but brings a hint from משלי, where the same words are tied to wine and meat.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even though there is no proof for this, there is a hint: "Do not be among wine-guzzlers, among gluttonous eaters of meat."
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה brings a supporting hint from another פסוק. It shows that the words זולל and סובא are used for meat and wine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק in דברים does not say "meat" or "wine" outright, so the משנה calls this only a זכר לדבר, a hint, not a ראיה. In משלי, סובא appears next to wine and זולל next to meat. This supports reading the Torah's words that way.

keyTerms.meaning: a real proof for the matter
a hint or reminder for the matter, weaker than a proof

steps.whatToRemember: "זולל וסבא" is understood as meat and wine. This is supported only by a hint (זכר לדבר) from משלי, not a full proof.

phrases.aramaic: וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין רְאָיָה לַדָּבָר,
phrases.english: And even though there is no proof for the matter,
there is a hint for the matter,
as it is stated: "Do not be among wine-guzzlers,
among gluttonous eaters of meat."
phrases.notes: משלי 23:20

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין רְאָיָה לַדָּבָר זֵכֶר לַדָּבָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports step 4's reading of "זולל וסבא" as meat and wine.
steps.raayaObject: That "זולל וסבא" in דברים refers to eating meat and drinking wine.
steps.raayaSupportSource: משלי 23:20, where סובאי is paired with wine and זוללי with meat.

steps.title: How much is a תרטימר?
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא figures out that a תרטימר is half a מנה, because רבי יוסי doubles both amounts.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: רבי זירא said: I don't know what this תרטימר is. But since רבי יוסי doubled the wine amount, he must also be doubling the meat amount. So a תרטימר is half a מנה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins by explaining an unclear word in the משנה, תרטימר. רבי זירא works out how much it is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא said half a לוג of wine, and רבי יוסי said a full לוג, which is double. רבי זירא reasons that רבי יוסי doubles the meat too. So the תנא קמא's תרטימר must be half of רבי יוסי's מנה.

keyTerms.meaning: An amount of meat named in the משנה; here worked out to be half a מנה
A measure of weight; רבי יוסי's amount of meat

phrases.english: GEMARA: Rabbi Zeira says:
This tarteimar, I do not know what it is,
phrases.notes: This is the meat amount from the משנה back in step 2.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא מִתּוֹךְ שֶׁכָּפַל רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּיַיִן,
phrases.english: but since Rabbi Yosei doubled the amount of wine,
phrases.notes: The first opinion said half a לוג and רבי יוסי said a full לוג, which is double.

phrases.english: it turns out he doubles for the meat as well,
and it turns out that a tarteimar is half a maneh.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא on the new משנה by explaining an unclear word from step 2.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A תרטימר equals half a מנה, worked out from the fact that רבי יוסי doubles the wine amount.

steps.title: He must buy the meat and wine cheaply
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא says the son is only liable if he buys cheap meat and wine, learned from the word זולל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חנן בר מולדה said in the name of רב הונא: He is not liable unless he buys meat cheaply and eats it, and wine cheaply and drinks it, as it says: 'זולל וסבא'.
steps.whatsHappening: A new rule is added about how the son gets his meat and wine: he must buy it at a cheap price.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word זולל sounds like זול, which means cheap. So רב הונא reads the פסוק as hinting that the son buys his food cheaply.

keyTerms.meaning: 'A glutton and a drunkard', the words of the פסוק about the בן סורר ומורה

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב חָנָן בַּר מוֹלָדָה אָמַר רַב הוּנָא:
phrases.english: Rav Ḥanan bar Molada says that Rav Huna says:

phrases.aramaic: אֵינוֹ חַיָּיב עַד שֶׁיִּקַּח בָּשָׂר בְּזוֹל וְיֹאכַל,
phrases.english: He is not liable unless he buys meat cheaply and eats it,
and buys wine cheaply and drinks it,
as it is written: “A glutton and a drunkard.”
phrases.notes: דברים 21:20. The word זולל sounds like זול, which means cheap.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חָנָן בַּר מוֹלָדָה אָמַר רַב הוּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the amount of food to how the food is bought.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: He is liable only if he buys the meat and wine cheaply, learned from the word זולל.

steps.title: Raw meat and undiluted wine
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא adds that the son is only liable if he eats 'raw' meat and drinks 'undiluted' wine.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חנן בר מולדה also said in the name of רב הונא: He is not liable unless he eats raw meat and drinks undiluted wine.
steps.whatsHappening: A second rule from the same speaker: the meat must be raw and the wine must be unmixed. This sets up the challenge that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This narrows the case to a wild, greedy way of eating and drinking. As we will see, it seems to clash with another teaching.

keyTerms.meaning: Undiluted wine, not mixed with water

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַב חָנָן בַּר מוֹלָדָה אָמַר רַב הוּנָא:
phrases.english: And Rav Ḥanan bar Molada says that Rav Huna says:

phrases.aramaic: אֵינוֹ חַיָּיב עַד שֶׁיֹּאכַל בָּשָׂר חַי
phrases.english: He is not liable unless he eats raw meat
and drinks undiluted wine.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַב חָנָן בַּר מוֹלָדָה אָמַר רַב הוּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second statement from the same speaker, adding another condition.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: He is liable only for raw meat and undiluted wine.

steps.title: But רבה and רב יוסף say raw meat does not count
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב הונא: רבה and רב יוסף say raw meat and undiluted wine do NOT make him a בן סורר ומורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that so? But רבה and רב יוסף both say: If he ate raw meat and drank undiluted wine, he does not become a בן סורר ומורה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the last rule by quoting רבה and רב יוסף, who say the exact opposite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא says he is liable ONLY for raw meat and undiluted wine. רבה and רב יוסף say raw meat and undiluted wine do NOT make him liable. Both cannot be true as they stand.

phrases.english: Is that so?

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא רַבָּה וְרַב יוֹסֵף דְּאָמְרִי תַּרְוַויְיהוּ:
phrases.english: But don't Rabba and Rav Yosef both say:

phrases.aramaic: אָכַל בָּשָׂר חַי וְשָׁתָה יַיִן חַי
phrases.english: If he ate raw meat and drank undiluted wine
he does not become a stubborn and rebellious son!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִינִי? וְהָא רַבָּה וְרַב יוֹסֵף דְּאָמְרִי תַּרְוַויְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב הונא's second rule from step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's rule that he is liable only for raw meat and undiluted wine.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבה and רב יוסף rule the opposite: raw meat and undiluted wine do not make him a בן סורר ומורה.

steps.title: רבינא: half-cooked meat and half-mixed wine
steps.stepSummary: רבינא explains that רב הונא meant meat that is only partly cooked and wine that is only partly mixed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: 'Undiluted wine' means wine that is mixed but not properly mixed. 'Raw meat' means meat that is cooked but not properly cooked, like the singed meat that thieves eat.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא answers the challenge by explaining what רב הונא meant by 'raw' and 'undiluted'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Fully raw meat and fully unmixed wine do not count, as רבה and רב יוסף said. רב הונא's words mean food in between: half-cooked meat and half-mixed wine. That is the kind that makes him liable, so the two teachings no longer clash.

keyTerms.meaning: Mixed but not mixed, only partly diluted
Cooked but not cooked, only partly cooked

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think רבינא is saying רב הונא was wrong. He keeps both teachings: totally raw does not count (רבה and רב יוסף), and half-done does count (רב הונא).

phrases.english: Ravina said:
“Undiluted wine” means diluted but not properly diluted;
“raw meat” means cooked but not properly cooked,
like the scorched meat that thieves eat.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבִינָא: יַיִן חַי – מְזִיג וְלָא מְזִיג
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining terms: 'raw' and 'undiluted' mean partly done, not fully raw.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב הונא seemed to mean totally raw meat and totally unmixed wine, which clashes with רבה and רב יוסף.
steps.terutzMaskana: Totally raw or unmixed does not count. Half-cooked meat and half-mixed wine does make him liable.

steps.title: Salted meat and fresh wine don't count
steps.stepSummary: רבה and רב יוסף say salted meat and wine straight from the press do not make him a בן סורר ומורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה and רב יוסף both say: If he ate salted meat and drank wine from his winepress, he does not become a בן סורר ומורה.
steps.whatsHappening: Another rule from רבה and רב יוסף lists more kinds of meat and wine that do not count.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Heavily salted meat and wine that is not yet finished are not treated as real meat and wine for this law. So eating them does not make him liable.

keyTerms.meaning: Wine from his winepress, fresh wine not yet finished

phrases.english: Rabba and Rav Yosef both say:
If he ate salted meat
or drank wine from his winepress,
phrases.notes: This is fresh wine that has not finished becoming wine yet.

phrases.english: he does not become a stubborn and rebellious son.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּה וְרַב יוֹסֵף דְּאָמְרִי תַּרְוַויְיהוּ: אָכַל בָּשָׂר מָלִיחַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the raw-meat discussion, adds more kinds of meat and wine that do not count.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Salted meat and fresh wine from the press do not make him a בן סורר ומורה.

steps.title: The same idea on ערב תשעה באב
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a משנה and a ברייתא about ערב תשעה באב. Meat and wine are forbidden there, but salted meat and fresh wine are allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in a משנה elsewhere: On ערב תשעה באב a person may not eat two cooked dishes, and may not eat meat or drink wine. And a ברייתא taught: But he may eat salted meat and drink wine from his winepress.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a similar case from the laws of ערב תשעה באב, where the same two foods are also left out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On ערב תשעה באב, meat and wine are forbidden, yet salted meat and fresh wine are allowed. That shows these foods are not treated as real 'meat' and 'wine'. This matches the rule of רבה and רב יוסף in step 11.

keyTerms.meaning: We learned in a משנה elsewhere
The day before the fast of תשעה באב

steps.whatToRemember: Salted meat and wine fresh from the press are not counted as real 'meat' and 'wine'. That is true for a בן סורר ומורה, and on ערב תשעה באב too.

phrases.english: We learned there, in a mishna:
phrases.notes: תענית 26b.

phrases.english: On the eve of the Ninth of Av
a person may not eat two cooked dishes,

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא יֹאכַל בָּשָׂר, וְלֹא יִשְׁתֶּה יַיִן.
phrases.english: and he may not eat meat, and he may not drink wine.
And a tanna taught in a baraita:
But he may eat salted meat
and drink wine from his winepress.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a parallel case that fits the rule of step 11.
steps.raayaObject: That salted meat and fresh wine are not treated as real meat and wine.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה in תענית about ערב תשעה באב, together with the ברייתא that allows salted meat and wine from the press.

steps.title: How long must meat be salted?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how long meat must sit in salt before it counts as 'salted meat' that is allowed on ערב תשעה באב.
steps.simpleTranslation: Salted meat: for how long?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is asking a follow-up question on the משנה and ברייתא about ערב תשעה באב that were just brought. This question sets up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 12 said salted meat is allowed on ערב תשעה באב. That raises the question of how long the meat must be salted before it stops counting as regular meat. The next step gives the exact measure.

phrases.english: With salted meat, up to how long?
phrases.notes: This is about the salted meat allowed on ערב תשעה באב from the last step: how long must it be salted?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the exact measure of a term used in the source from step 12.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The length of salting that makes meat count as 'salted meat'.

steps.title: Meat stays regular meat as long as it is like שלמים
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא בר כהנא answers that meat still counts as regular meat for as long as שלמים could still be eaten.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנינא בר כהנא says: As long as it is like שלמים.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חנינא בר כהנא gives the measure. Salted meat is still treated as regular meat as long as it is within the time for eating שלמים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שלמים may be eaten for two days and one night. Meat salted for less time than that still counts as regular meat and is forbidden on ערב תשעה באב. Once that time has passed, it counts as 'salted meat' and is allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: Peace-offerings, which may be eaten for two days and one night

phrases.english: Rabbi Chanina bar Kahana said:
As long as it is like peace-offerings.
phrases.notes: שלמים can be eaten for two days and one night. While the meat is within that time, it still counts as regular meat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 13.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Meat counts as regular meat for as long as שלמים could be eaten. After that, it counts as salted meat.

steps.title: How new is 'wine from the press'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for how long new wine counts as 'wine from the press.'
steps.simpleTranslation: And wine from its press: for how long?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks the same kind of question about the wine. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 12 said fresh wine from the press is allowed on ערב תשעה באב. Now the גמרא wants to know how long wine keeps that 'fresh' status.

keyTerms.meaning: Wine straight from its winepress (new, unfermented wine)

phrases.english: And wine from its press, up to how long?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks the parallel question about wine, after the question about meat.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How long wine counts as 'wine from the press.'

steps.title: As long as the wine is still fermenting
steps.stepSummary: Wine counts as 'from the press' for as long as it is still fermenting.
steps.simpleTranslation: As long as it is fermenting.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that wine is 'from the press' for as long as it is still bubbling and fermenting.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This answer gives a sign (fermenting) rather than a number of days. The next step adds a source that turns this into a number.

phrases.english: As long as it is fermenting.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 15.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Wine is 'from the press' while it is still fermenting.

steps.title: A ברייתא shows that fermenting lasts three days
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא about uncovered liquids teaches that the first fermenting of wine lasts three days.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it was taught: Fermenting wine is not subject to the rule of uncovered liquids. And how long is its fermenting? Three days.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to show how long 'fermenting' lasts. The answer is three days.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא is about גילוי, the rule against drinking liquids that were left uncovered. It says fermenting wine is not included in that rule, and that fermenting lasts three days. This puts a number on step 16: for ערב תשעה באב, wine counts as 'from the press' for three days.

keyTerms.meaning: And it was taught in a ברייתא
Uncovered liquids, which are forbidden in case a snake drank from them

phrases.english: And it was taught:

phrases.aramaic: יַיִן תּוֹסֵס אֵין בּוֹ מִשּׁוּם גִּילּוּי.
phrases.english: Fermenting wine is not subject to the rule of uncovered liquids.
phrases.notes: Uncovered drinks were forbidden in case a snake left venom in them. Bubbling wine is not included in that worry.

phrases.english: And how long is its fermenting? Three days.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָתַנְיָא: יַיִן תּוֹסֵס אֵין בּוֹ מִשּׁוּם גִּילּוּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports step 16 and gives a number of days for 'fermenting.'
steps.raayaObject: How long wine is 'fermenting,' and so counts as 'from the press.'
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about uncovered liquids: the first fermenting lasts three days.

steps.title: What about בן סורר ומורה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether the same measures apply to בן סורר ומורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here, what?
steps.whatsHappening: The measures so far were for ערב תשעה באב. Now the גמרא asks what the measures are for בן סורר ומורה, which is the main topic. This short question sets up the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 11 said salted meat and wine from the press do not make a boy a בן סורר ומורה, and step 12 proved this from ערב תשעה באב. That raises a fair question: do the ערב תשעה באב time limits carry over to בן סורר ומורה?

phrases.english: Here, what is the measure?
phrases.notes: 'Here' means the case of בן סורר ומורה, as opposed to ערב תשעה באב.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from the measures for ערב תשעה באב back to בן סורר ומורה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the measures for salted meat and new wine are the same for בן סורר ומורה.

steps.title: Different reasons lead to different measures
steps.stepSummary: On ערב תשעה באב the issue is שמחה, while for בן סורר ומורה it is the boy being drawn to the food. So for him, even slightly salted meat does not count, and wine counts as 'from the press' for forty days.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, the reason is joy; as long as the meat is like שלמים, it still brings joy. Here, the reason is being drawn to it, and with even a little change he will not be drawn. And wine: up to forty days.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the measures for בן סורר ומורה are different, because each rule has a different reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On ערב תשעה באב, meat is forbidden because it brings שמחה, and salted meat still brings joy while it is like שלמים. A בן סורר ומורה is punished because he is drawn after meat and wine. Even a little salting spoils the taste enough that he won't be drawn to it, and wine does not draw him in until it is forty days old.

keyTerms.meaning: With any amount, even a little

steps.whatToRemember: The same words ('salted meat,' 'wine from the press') get different time limits because the reason behind each law is different: שמחה on ערב תשעה באב, being drawn in for בן סורר ומורה.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not assume the three-day and 'like שלמים' measures apply to בן סורר ומורה. For him, even slightly salted meat does not count, and wine counts as 'from the press' for much longer, forty days.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a common method in the גמרא: to define a term, look at the reason behind the law it appears in.

phrases.english: There, it is because of joy;
as long as it is like peace-offerings,
it also has joy in it.
Here, it is because of being drawn after it,
and with even a little, he is not drawn.
phrases.notes: He means that once the meat is even a little salted, the boy won't crave it.

phrases.english: And wine: up to forty days.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 18 by showing the reasons for the two laws are different.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: For בן סורר ומורה, even slightly salted meat does not count, and wine is 'from the press' until forty days, because the rule there is about being drawn to the food, not about joy.

steps.title: Wine was created to comfort mourners and reward the wicked
steps.stepSummary: רב חנן teaches that wine was created only to comfort mourners and to pay the wicked their reward in this world, based on a פסוק in משלי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חנן said: Wine was created in the world only to comfort mourners and to pay reward to the wicked, as it says: 'Give strong drink to the one who is perishing, and wine to the bitter of soul.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a general teaching about wine. רב חנן says wine has only two purposes, and he brings a פסוק for both.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק has two parts. 'The one who is perishing' refers to the wicked, who receive their reward, wine, in this world. 'The bitter of soul' refers to mourners, whom wine comforts.

keyTerms.meaning: To pay the wicked their reward
Bitter of soul, people in deep sorrow

phrases.english: Rav Chanan said:
Wine was not created in the world
except to comfort mourners,
and to pay reward to the wicked,
as it is said: 'Give strong drink to the one who is perishing,'
phrases.notes: משלי 31:6

phrases.english: 'and wine to the bitter of soul.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חָנָן: לֹא נִבְרָא יַיִן בָּעוֹלָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the legal measures for wine to a general teaching about wine.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Wine was created only to comfort mourners and to reward the wicked, based on משלי 31:6.

steps.title: רבי יצחק: Wine reddens the faces of the wicked now and shames them later
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק explains 'Look not upon wine when it is red' to mean that wine makes the wicked red-faced in this world and pale with shame in עולם הבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק says: What does the verse 'Look not upon wine when it is red' mean? Do not look at wine that makes the faces of the wicked red in this world but makes their faces white in עולם הבא.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יצחק gives a new explanation of a פסוק in משלי that warns against wine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He reads 'red' as the flushed face of a drinker. The red face of pleasure now turns into a pale face of shame in עולם הבא. Wine's short-term enjoyment leads to a long-term cost.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzchak says:
What is the meaning of that which is written:
"Look not upon wine when it is red"?
phrases.notes: משלי 23:31

phrases.english: Look not upon wine that reddens
the faces of the wicked in this world,
and whitens their faces in the World to Come.
phrases.notes: Whitening the face means making someone pale with embarrassment.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the series of teachings about wine that began with רב חנן in step 20.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Wine gives the wicked a red face of pleasure in this world and a pale face of shame in עולם הבא.

steps.title: רבא: Wine ends in bloodshed
steps.stepSummary: רבא reads the same פסוק differently: hidden inside 'יתאדם' is the word דם, blood, so wine leads to bloodshed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא says: 'Look not upon wine when it is red' means: Do not look at wine, because its end is blood.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא offers a second explanation of the same פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יצחק read 'red' as the color of the face. רבא hears the word דם inside יתאדם. Drinking can lead a person to kill or be killed.

phrases.english: Rava says:
"Look not upon wine when it is red" means:
Look not upon wine, whose end is blood.
phrases.notes: רבא hears the word דם, blood, inside the word יתאדם.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא אָמַר: אַל תֵּרֶא יַיִן כִּי יִתְאַדָּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different explanation of the same פסוק that רבי יצחק explained in step 21.

steps.title: רב כהנא: Wine can make a person a leader or a pauper
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא notes that the word for wine is spelled תירש but read תירוש. If a person merits, he becomes a ראש (head). If not, he becomes a רש (poor man).
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא points out a contradiction: It is written 'תירש' but we read 'תירוש'. If he merits, he becomes a head. If he does not merit, he becomes poor.
steps.whatsHappening: רב כהנא learns a lesson from the difference between how a word for wine is spelled and how it is read.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The spelled form תירש holds the word רש, poor. The read form תירוש holds the word ראש, head. The two forms show the two possible results of wine: drinking with control raises a person up, and drinking too much ruins him.

keyTerms.meaning: It is written one way, and we read it another way
If he merits / if he does not merit

phrases.english: Rav Kahana raises a contradiction:
phrases.notes: He is setting how the word is spelled against how it is read.

phrases.english: It is written "tirash"
phrases.notes: Spelled without a ו, in a פסוק in ירמיהו 31:12.

phrases.english: but we read it "tirosh".
If he merits, he becomes a head;
if he does not merit, he becomes poor.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב כָּהֲנָא רָמֵי: כְּתִיב תִּירָשׁ וְקָרֵינַן תִּירוֹשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another teaching about wine, this one showing it can have a good result as well as a bad one.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Wine makes a deserving person a leader and an undeserving person poor.

steps.title: רבא: Wine can gladden a person or drive him crazy
steps.stepSummary: רבא notes that the word for 'gladdens' can be read with a ש (makes desolate) or with a ש with the dot on the left (makes happy). If a person merits, wine makes him happy. If not, it makes him desolate.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא raises a contradiction: It is written 'יְשַׁמַּח' but we read 'יְשַׂמַּח'. If he merits, it gladdens him. If he does not merit, it makes him desolate.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא makes the same kind of point as רב כהנא, using a different פסוק about wine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The letters of ישמח can be read as ישמח with a שׁ, which sounds like 'make desolate' or 'drive crazy', or as ישמח with a שׂ, 'gladden'. The two readings again show wine's two possible results, depending on whether the person merits.

phrases.english: Rava raises a contradiction:
It is written "yeshamach"
phrases.notes: The letters can be read with a שׁ, which sounds like 'make desolate'.

phrases.english: but we read it "yesamach" (gladdens).
phrases.notes: תהלים 104:15

phrases.english: If he merits, it gladdens him;
if he does not merit, it makes him desolate.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא רָמֵי: כְּתִיב יְשַׁמַּח וְקָרֵינַן יְשַׂמַּח
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Parallels רב כהנא's teaching in step 23 with the same 'merits / does not merit' structure.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Wine gladdens a deserving person and drives an undeserving person to ruin.

steps.title: רבא's saying shows that wine in the right measure makes a person wise
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא links רבא's teaching to his other saying: 'Wine and fragrant spices made me wise.'
steps.simpleTranslation: And this is what רבא meant when he said: Wine and fragrant spices make me wise.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא connects רבא's teaching to another saying of his that shows the good side of wine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 24 said wine gladdens a person who merits. רבא's saying confirms that drinking with control really helps a person and even sharpens his mind.

keyTerms.meaning: And this is what he meant when he said

phrases.english: And that is what Rava said:
Wine and fragrant spices make me wise.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the 'if he merits, it gladdens him' half of step 24.
steps.raayaObject: That controlled drinking of wine benefits a person.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבא's own saying: חמרא וריחני פקחין.
steps.whatToRemember: Wine is two-sided: in the right measure it raises a person up, gladdens him and sharpens him. Too much of it makes him poor and desolate.

steps.title: רבי חנינא asks about the פסוק listing the troubles of drinkers
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא, quoted by רב עמרם, asks for the meaning of the פסוק in משלי that lists woe, quarrels and wounds, and then mentions those who linger over wine.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב עמרם, son of רבי שמעון בר אבא, says that רבי חנינא says: What does the verse mean: 'Who has woe? Who has alas? Who has quarrels? Who has complaints? Who has wounds for nothing? Who has redness of eyes? Those who linger over wine, those who come to seek mixed wine'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets up the next teaching by quoting a long פסוק and asking what it means. The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק first lists six troubles and then names the drinkers. The question is how the two halves connect: are the troubles the result of drinking, or do they describe who drinks?

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב עַמְרָם בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בַּר אַבָּא,
phrases.english: Rav Amram, son of Rabbi Shimon bar Abba, says
that Rabbi Chanina says:
What is the meaning of that which is written:
"Who has woe? Who has alas?
Who has quarrels? Who has complaints?
Who has wounds for nothing?
Who has redness of eyes? (and so on)
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the 'and so on' in round brackets.

phrases.english: Those who linger over the wine,
those who come to seek mixed wine"?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב עַמְרָם בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בַּר אַבָּא, אָמַר רַבִּי חֲנִינָא: מַאי דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to a new פסוק about the harm of wine.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How the list of troubles in the פסוק connects to the drinkers named at its end.

steps.title: רב דימי: The פסוק works read forward and backward
steps.stepSummary: רב דימי reports that in ארץ ישראל they said this פסוק can be explained meaningfully from beginning to end and also from end to beginning.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רב דימי came, he said: They say in the West: This verse can be explained by someone who reads it from beginning to end, and also by someone who reads it from end to beginning.
steps.whatsHappening: רב דימי answers the question by saying the פסוק can be read in both directions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Read forward, it asks who has woe and quarrels and answers: those who linger over wine. So drinking causes these troubles. Read backward, it asks who lingers over wine and answers: people already full of quarrels and complaints. So troubled people turn to drink. Both readings are true.

keyTerms.meaning: When (he) came (from ארץ ישראל to בבל)
From its beginning to its end

phrases.english: When Rav Dimi came, he said:
They say in the West:
phrases.notes: 'The West' is ארץ ישראל, which lies west of בבל.

phrases.english: This verse, one who expounds it
from its beginning to its end, it can be expounded,
and from its end to its beginning, it can be expounded.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי אֲתָא רַב דִּימִי אֲמַר: אָמְרִי בְּמַעְרְבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי חנינא's question from step 26.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק can be read both forward and backward. Wine brings troubles, and troubled people drink.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows a two-way connection: drinking leads to quarrels and injuries, and people caught up in such troubles are the ones who turn to wine.

steps.title: Thirteen words with a ו׳ in the story of נח's wine
steps.stepSummary: A visitor from the גליל teaches that the פסוקים describing נח's drunkenness contain thirteen words that start with ו׳.
steps.simpleTranslation: A visitor from the גליל taught: the letter ו׳ appears thirteen times in the story of wine. 'And נח began to be a man of the earth, and he planted a vineyard, and he drank of the wine, and became drunk, and was uncovered in his tent. And חם, father of כנען, saw his father's nakedness, and told his two brothers outside. And שם and יפת took the garment, and placed it on both their shoulders, and walked backward, and covered their father's nakedness, and their faces...' 'And נח woke from his wine, and knew what his youngest son had done to him.'
steps.whatsHappening: A new teacher brings one more lesson about how harmful wine can be. He uses the story of נח getting drunk after the flood.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He counts thirteen words in the story that begin with וַיִּ or a similar opening. Each one starts with the sound וַי, which sounds like 'woe'. So the story itself, word by word, cries out how much trouble wine brought.

keyTerms.meaning: A visitor (or traveler) from the גליל
The letter ו׳ (plural), here the ones that begin words

steps.confusionAlert: Not every ו׳ in the פסוק is counted. Only the thirteen words that begin with וַיְ/וַיִּ are counted, such as ויחל, ויטע and וישת. Words like 'וּפְנֵיהֶם' are not part of the count.

phrases.english: A visitor from the Galilee taught:
Thirteen times the letter vav is stated in the passage about wine:
phrases.notes: Each counted word starts with וַי, which sounds like 'woe'.

phrases.english: "And Noah began to be a man of the soil,
phrases.notes: בראשית 9:20-24

phrases.english: and he planted a vineyard, and he drank of the wine,
and became drunk, and was uncovered inside his tent.

phrases.aramaic: וַיַּרְא חָם אֲבִי כְנַעַן אֵת עֶרְוַת אָבִיו,
phrases.english: And Ham, the father of Canaan, saw the nakedness of his father,
and told his two brothers outside.
And Shem and Japheth took the garment,

phrases.aramaic: וַיָּשִׂימוּ עַל שְׁכֶם שְׁנֵיהֶם, וַיֵּלְכוּ אֲחֹרַנִּית,
phrases.english: and placed it on both their shoulders, and walked backward,

phrases.aramaic: וַיְכַסּוּ אֵת עֶרְוַת אֲבִיהֶם וּפְנֵיהֶם וְגוֹ׳״,
phrases.english: and covered the nakedness of their father, and their faces, etc."
"And Noah awoke from his wine,

phrases.aramaic: וַיֵּדַע אֵת אֲשֶׁר עָשָׂה לוֹ בְּנוֹ הַקָּטָן״.
phrases.english: and knew what his youngest son had done to him."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another teaching on the dangers of wine, continuing the theme of steps 23-27.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The story of נח's drunkenness has thirteen words beginning with וַי, hinting at 'woe' brought by wine.

steps.title: What did חם do to נח?
steps.stepSummary: רב and שמואל disagree. One says חם castrated נח, and the other says he sodomized him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב and שמואל: one says he castrated him, and one says he sodomized him.
steps.whatsHappening: The פסוק said נח knew 'what his youngest son had done to him'. Now רב and שמואל argue about what exactly that act was.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק only hints that חם did something to נח and does not say what it was. One opinion says חם castrated נח, so נח could no longer have children. The other says חם committed a forbidden relation with him. The גמרא does not say which opinion belongs to רב and which to שמואל.

keyTerms.meaning: One said... and one said (an unassigned מחלוקת)

phrases.english: Rav and Shmuel disagree:
one says Ham castrated him,
and one says Ham sodomized him.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב וּשְׁמוּאֵל: חַד אָמַר סֵרְסוֹ, וְחַד אָמַר רְבָעוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Picks up the last words of the quoted פסוק and opens a new discussion about them.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מחלוקת: either חם castrated נח, or he sodomized him.

steps.title: Why the castration opinion makes sense: a fourth son for a fourth son
steps.stepSummary: The castration opinion is supported by the fact that נח cursed חם's fourth son, כנען.
steps.simpleTranslation: The one who says he castrated him: since חם ruined נח regarding a fourth son, נח cursed him through his fourth son.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now explains where the first opinion gets its idea from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: נח had three sons and could have had a fourth. By castrating him, חם took that fourth son away. So the punishment matched the crime: נח cursed כנען, who was חם's fourth son.

keyTerms.meaning: The one who says (a given opinion)

phrases.english: The one who says Ham castrated him reasons:
since he ruined Noah regarding a fourth son,
phrases.notes: He means that חם stopped נח from ever having a fourth son, after שם, חם and יפת.

phrases.english: Noah cursed him through his fourth son.
phrases.notes: חם's sons were כוש, מצרים, פוט and כנען (בראשית 10:6). כנען was the fourth, and he is the one נח cursed.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאן דְּאָמַר סֵרְסוֹ: מִתּוֹךְ שֶׁקִּלְקְלוֹ בָּרְבִיעִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reasoning for the first side of the מחלוקת.
steps.raayaObject: The opinion that חם castrated נח.
steps.raayaSupportSource: נח cursed חם's fourth son, כנען, as a punishment that matched losing his own fourth son.

steps.title: Why the other opinion makes sense: 'and he saw' in two places
steps.stepSummary: The second opinion learns from the word 'וַיַּרְא' (and he saw), which also appears in the story of שכם and דינה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the one who says he sodomized him learns 'and he saw' from 'and he saw'. Here it is written: 'And חם, father of כנען, saw his father's nakedness.' And there it is written: 'And שכם son of חמור saw her...'
steps.whatsHappening: Now the גמרא explains the source for the second opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'וַיַּרְא' appears about חם and also about שכם. In the שכם story, 'seeing' led straight to a forbidden relation with דינה. Comparing the two places, this opinion reads 'seeing' in the נח story the same way.

keyTerms.meaning: Learns (one פסוק from another, through a shared word)
It is written here... and it is written there (the standard way of comparing two פסוקים)

phrases.english: And the one who says Ham sodomized him:
learns "and he saw" from "and he saw."

phrases.aramaic: כְּתִיב הָכָא: ״וַיַּרְא חָם אֲבִי כְנַעַן אֵת עֶרְוַת אָבִיו״,
phrases.english: It is written here: "And Ham, the father of Canaan, saw the nakedness of his father,"

phrases.aramaic: וּכְתִיב הָתָם: ״וַיַּרְא אוֹתָהּ שְׁכֶם בֶּן חֲמוֹר וְגוֹ׳״.
phrases.english: and it is written there: "And Shechem, son of Hamor, saw her, etc."
phrases.notes: בראשית 34:2. The rest of the פסוק says he took her and lay with her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reasoning for the second side of the מחלוקת, parallel to step 30.
steps.raayaObject: The opinion that חם sodomized נח.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The shared word 'וַיַּרְא' in the story of שכם and דינה, where seeing led to a forbidden relation.

steps.title: Why curse the fourth son?
steps.stepSummary: The fourth-son curse fits the castration opinion. But according to the other opinion, why didn't נח just curse חם himself?
steps.simpleTranslation: It works well for the one who says he castrated him: that is why נח cursed him through the fourth son. But for the one who says he sodomized him, what is special about the fourth son? נח should have cursed חם directly!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the second opinion. It asks why that opinion cannot explain a detail in the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The castration opinion explains neatly why כנען, the fourth son, was cursed. If חם only sodomized נח, nothing about a 'fourth' was taken away. So it seems נח should have cursed חם himself rather than his son.

keyTerms.meaning: It works well for... but for... (sets up a challenge to one side)
What is different / what is special about
He should have cursed him directly

phrases.english: It makes sense according to the one who says he castrated him,
that because of this Noah cursed him through his fourth son.
But according to the one who says he sodomized him,
what is special about the fourth son?
He should have cursed Ham directly!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Compares the two explanations and finds a problem with the second one.
steps.kashyaTarget: The opinion that חם sodomized נח (step 31).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Only castration explains why the curse fell on the fourth son. Without it, נח should have cursed חם himself.

steps.title: Both things happened
steps.stepSummary: The second opinion holds that חם did both acts, so the fourth-son curse still makes sense.
steps.simpleTranslation: This and that both happened.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge in three short words: חם did both things to נח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The second opinion does not deny the castration. It agrees that חם castrated נח, which explains the curse on the fourth son. It simply adds that he also sodomized him. So the difference between the opinions is only whether the second act happened as well.
steps.whatToRemember: Everyone agrees חם castrated נח, which is why כנען, the fourth son, was cursed. One opinion adds that חם also sodomized him, learned from the word 'וַיַּרְא'.

phrases.english: This and that both happened.
phrases.notes: The second opinion agrees about the castration and adds the other act on top of it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 32.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Expanding the opinion: it includes both acts, not just one.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought the second opinion held only that חם sodomized נח, which leaves the fourth-son curse unexplained.
steps.terutzMaskana: The second opinion holds that חם did both acts, so the castration explains the curse on the fourth son.

steps.title: ה׳ criticizes נח for planting a vineyard
steps.stepSummary: On the פסוק 'נח began to be a man of the land and planted a vineyard,' רבי זכאי teaches that הקדוש ברוך הוא told נח he should have learned from אדם הראשון, whose downfall was caused only by wine.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'And נח began to be a man of the land, and he planted a vineyard.' רב חסדא said in the name of רב עוקבא (some say מר עוקבא), who said in the name of רבי זכאי: הקדוש ברוך הוא said to נח, 'נח, shouldn't you have learned from אדם הראשון, whose downfall came only through wine?'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a new פסוק about נח and brings a teaching that criticizes him for planting a vineyard first. ה׳ tells נח he should have learned a lesson from אדם הראשון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Of all the things נח could have planted after the flood, he chose a vineyard, and that led to his drunkenness. רבי זכאי says נח should have known better, because wine had already caused the first sin of mankind. This teaching assumes wine was involved in אדם's sin, and the גמרא explains that assumption in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: And he began (the opening word of the פסוק about נח)
A man of the land, a farmer
And some say (a different version of who said it)

phrases.english: "And Noah began to be a man of the land, and he planted a vineyard."
phrases.notes: בראשית 9:20

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא אָמַר רַב עוּקְבָא,
phrases.english: Rav Chisda said that Rav Ukva said,
and some say it was Mar Ukva,
who said that Rabbi Zakkai said:

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לְנֹחַ:
phrases.english: The Holy One, Blessed be He, said to Noah:
Noah, shouldn't you have learned
from Adam the first man,
whose downfall was caused only by wine?
phrases.notes: He means אדם: his sin and being sent out of גן עדן.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא אָמַר רַב עוּקְבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the argument about what חם did to נח and goes back to an earlier פסוק about נח planting a vineyard.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: נח was at fault for planting a vineyard. He should have learned from אדם הראשון that wine leads to sin.

steps.title: This follows the view that the forbidden tree was a grapevine
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that רבי זכאי's teaching follows the opinion that the tree אדם הראשון ate from was a grapevine.
steps.simpleTranslation: This teaching follows the one who says that the tree אדם הראשון ate from was a grapevine.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains which opinion רבי זכאי's teaching depends on. This also sets up the next step, where the source for that opinion is quoted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי זכאי said אדם's downfall came through wine. That only makes sense if the forbidden tree was a grapevine. So his teaching is tied to one side of a known question about what kind of tree it was.

keyTerms.meaning: In line with the one who says (this follows a certain opinion)

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying everyone agrees the tree was a grapevine. It is only saying that רבי זכאי's teaching fits that one opinion.

phrases.english: This is according to the one who says

phrases.aramaic: אוֹתוֹ אִילָן שֶׁאָכַל מִמֶּנּוּ אָדָם הָרִאשׁוֹן –
phrases.english: that the tree from which Adam the first man ate
was a grapevine.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Names the opinion that step 34's claim, that wine caused אדם's downfall, depends on.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי זכאי's teaching follows the opinion that the tree of knowledge was a grapevine.

steps.title: רבי מאיר says the tree was a grapevine
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא in which רבי מאיר says the tree אדם הראשון ate from was a grapevine.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught in a ברייתא: רבי מאיר says the tree that אדם הראשון ate from was a grapevine,
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the source for the opinion it just mentioned: a ברייתא quoting רבי מאיר. The sentence continues in the next section, which gives his reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 35 said there is someone who holds the tree was a grapevine. Here the גמרא shows who that is: רבי מאיר, in a ברייתא. This gives a real source behind רבי זכאי's idea that wine caused the first sin.

keyTerms.meaning: As it was taught in a ברייתא
A תנא whose opinion is quoted here

phrases.english: As it is taught in a baraita:
Rabbi Meir says,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹתוֹ אִילָן שֶׁאָכַל אָדָם הָרִאשׁוֹן מִמֶּנּוּ –
phrases.english: the tree that Adam the first man ate from
was a grapevine,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the opinion mentioned in step 35.
steps.raayaObject: The opinion that the tree of knowledge was a grapevine, which רבי זכאי's teaching depends on.
